set.presentation: A 67-year-old woman develops crushing substernal chest pain and breathlessness an hour after being robbed at knifepoint outside her shop. No prior heart disease; nonsmoker, normal lipids last year. BP 102/68, HR 104; soft apical systolic murmur, bibasilar crackles.

A 17-year-old basketball player faints during a sprint drill and recovers in seconds; for months hard exercise has brought on chest tightness. BP 124/72, HR 64; forceful sustained apex beat, S4, brisk carotid upstroke; harsh 3/6 systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, not radiating to the neck.

A 24-year-old man collapses playing soccer and is revived with one shock; for a year exercise has brought on palpitations and a pounding heart. A cousin died suddenly at 30. Since childhood the skin of his palms and soles has been thick and hard. BP 118/74; heart exam normal.
